claims.statement: The shared ArchUnit rule suites (ArchitectureTest, BasicArchitectureTest, DeterministicArdocoTest) and evaluation base classes (ConfigurationTestBase, ExpectedResults, EvaluationProject, EvaluationHelper) live in core/tests-base/src/main (not src/test) with compile-scoped ArchUnit/JUnit/metrics dependencies, so other modules consume them as a test-scoped tests-base jar; archunit.properties sets archRule.failOnEmptyShould=false so a rule matching nothing on a module's classpath does not fail that module.

ArchitectureTest enforces the product architecture: a layeredArchitecture rule over the layers Common, TextExtractor, ModelExtractor, RecommendationGenerator, ConnectionGenerator, Artemis, InconsistencyDetection, CodeTraceability, Pipeline, and Execution with per-layer access restrictions (Execution only accessed by Common; InconsistencyDetection only by Pipeline, Common, and Execution; the Artemis layer only by ConnectionGenerator, Pipeline, Execution, Common, InconsistencyDetection, and CodeTraceability), plus ordering/naming rules — execution classes are only used by execution/test code, Model-named classes only after model extraction (with the Artemis package an allowed consumer), classes whose name ends in Link only after the connection generator and confined to the tracelink/codetraceability/connectiongenerator packages, and Inconsistency-named classes only after inconsistency detection.

BasicArchitectureTest enforces cross-cutting rules: @Configurable fields may only be declared in AbstractConfigurable subclasses, TraceLink subclasses must be final, Jackson mappers may only be created or configured in JsonHandling (jacksonIsConfiguredGlobally covers ObjectMapper/subclass constructors and the builder/shared/rebuild methods) and Jackson 2 (com.fasterxml.jackson.core/databind) is banned outright by noJackson2 because ARDoCo uses Jackson 3 (tools.jackson), System.getenv may only be called by the Environment utility (noGetEnv), forEach/forEachOrdered must not be used on streams or lists, and interface methods must prefer Eclipse Collections over JDK List/Set/Map/Sorted* raw types outside ..metrics.. packages.

DeterministicArdocoTest keeps pipeline runs reproducible: classes not directly annotated @Deterministic must not access unordered JDK/Eclipse sets and maps (Set, HashSet, MutableSet, ImmutableSet, Sets, Map, HashMap, MutableMap, ImmutableMap, Maps) outside the ..tests../..metrics../..magika.. packages; HashMap/HashSet are forbidden in favor of linked versions; @NoHashCodeEquals-annotated classes must not implement equals/hashCode; classes directly implementing Comparable must implement both equals and hashCode; and sorted collections (fields and returns) may only be parameterized with Comparable types.

ConfigurationTestBase uses Reflections to enumerate every concrete, non-abstract AbstractConfigurable subclass under edu.kit.kastel.mcse.ardoco outside tests packages, validates that all @Configurable fields are neither final nor static, and prints the complete default configuration as key=value lines; it delegates assertions to abstract assertFalse/fail hooks that module subclasses such as tlr.tests.ConfigurationTest and id.tests.ConfigurationTest bind to JUnit.

tests-tlr and tests-inconsistency re-enable the shared ArchUnit suites by subclassing them in their own test trees with @AnalyzeClasses over edu.kit.kastel.mcse.ardoco core+tlr packages (tests-tlr) and core+tlr+id packages (tests-inconsistency), so the same rules are re-evaluated against each module's classpath and violations introduced in TLR or ID modules are caught in those modules.

ExpectedResults is a record of six minimum metrics (precision, recall, f1, accuracy, phiCoefficient, specificity); benchmark evaluations assert with assertTrue(metric >= minimum) inside Assertions.assertAll covering precision, recall, F1, accuracy, and the phi coefficient — so a regression in any single asserted metric fails the build — while specificity is carried and logged but not currently asserted.

EvaluationProject defines ten benchmark projects: MEDIASTORE, TEASTORE, TEAMMATES, BIGBLUEBUTTON, and JABREF with PCM model, SAD text, GitHub repository URL with pinned commit hash, and cached codeModel.acm; plus the code-focused ZENGARDEN, SCONS, BEETS, ROD, and CORONAWARNAPP whose architectureModelResource is a /benchmark/

/notAvailable placeholder and which are consumed by the class/datafile ArTEMiS tasks and LLM-based ID evaluations. getCodeModelFromResources loads the ACM fixture while getCodeDirectory shallow-clones the repository into $TMPDIR/ARDoCo/ via RepositoryHandler.shallowCloneRepository (depth-1 clone, unshallow plus checkout of the pinned commit when the fetched tip differs).

tests-base bundles a snapshot of the ardoco/benchmark datasets plus per-project filter configurations on its classpath (e.g. /benchmark/mediastore/... and /configurations/ms/filterlists_all.txt with folders ms, ts, tm, bbb, jabref), and EvaluationHelper materializes classpath resources into temporary files (deleteOnExit) because the extraction APIs take File arguments.

InconsistencyDetectionTask wraps an EvaluationProject and adds the ID evaluation inputs for the five classic projects: the *_UME.csv unmentioned-model-element gold standard (header and blank lines stripped), the sentence-to-architecture gold standard CSV, a per-project filter-list configuration, and its ExpectedResults minimums.

All benchmark comparisons compute metrics via ClassificationMetricsCalculator from the io.github.ardoco:metrics dependency (pulled in by tests-base) with an explicit confusion-matrix denominator: the number of sentences for the ID TEAM evaluation, sentences × architecture-model endpoints for SAD-SAM TLR, and code-model endpoints × architecture-model endpoints for SAM-Code TLR; code-based gold standards are enrolled first so package entries whose id ends in '/' expand into one gold link per code-model endpoint under that path.

tests-tlr and tests-inconsistency declare tests-base as a test-scoped dependency and bind maven-failsafe-plugin (root POM version 3.5.6, integration-test and verify goals at the integration-test phase), so mvn verify runs both Surefire unit/ArchUnit tests and Failsafe *IT.java integration tests; the module-scoped recipes are mvn -pl tlr clean verify and mvn -pl inconsistency-detection clean verify.

The TLR integration tests are environment-gated and largely disabled: SwattrIT and SwattrAiIT run unconditionally (SwattrAiIT feeds pre-generated LLM component listings as ModelFormat.COMPONENT_LISTING with metric assertions disabled), while ArdocodeIT, ArcotlIT, and TransarcIT are @Disabled(temporarily disabled) — ArcotlIT/TransarcIT still offer full-clone variants enabled by the testCodeFull environment variable that first remove the cached code directory via RepositoryHandler.removeRepository and then evaluate from a fresh pinned-commit clone; ArtemisIT, ArtemisInTransarcIT, ExArchIT, and ArtemisInExArchIT are @Disabled(Only for manual execution) and additionally LLM-gated (OPENAI_API_KEY or OLLAMA_HOST assumed in @BeforeAll) with CI-skipping for ArtemisIT and the ExArch ITs.

AbstractArdocoIT.averageAndLog averages repeated runs per metric and logs mean ± stddev to cope with LLM nondeterminism. The manual-only ArtemisIT parameterizes over all LargeLanguageModel values (including generic variants) × the three ArtemisEvaluationProject families via @MethodSource, asserting against those enums' uniform 0.420 minimums; setting the env variable mutipleRuns disables its four single-run tests and enables multi-run variants that execute NUMBER_OF_RUNS = 5 repetitions aggregated by averageAndLog. ArtemisInTransarcIT runs per TransarcEvaluationProject with the NER LLM fixed to GPT_5, only logs results, and has an analogous mutipleRuns multi-run variant. A @BeforeAll assumption in both classes requires OPENAI_API_KEY or OLLAMA_HOST, and ArtemisIT additionally assumes CI is unset.

HoldBackRunResultsProducer produces one base run over the full model stored under the null key plus one run per architecture component, each removing exactly that component; HoldBackArCoTLModelProvider extracts the PCM model once and supplies a PipelineAgent whose extractor returns the initial model minus the current hold-back (a negative index holds nothing back); every run is an AnonymousRunner pipeline TextPreprocessingAgent → TextExtraction → hold-back model provider → RecommendationGenerator → ConnectionGenerator → InconsistencyChecker, or InconsistencyBaseline for the baseline variant, configured from the project's filter-list file.

The TEAM evaluation (order 1) compares the sentence numbers of detected TextEntityAbsentFromModelInconsistency entries against the gold-standard sentences that mention the removed element (from the sentence-to-architecture gold standard via getGoldstandardForArchitectureModel) using the '<sentenceNumber> -> <componentName>' string format so false positives with the same sentence number but a different component name are distinguished; it aggregates per-run results with the micro-average via ClassificationMetricsCalculator and asserts them against the project's ExpectedResults minimums in checkResults; base runs (null key) are excluded from scoring and only logged.

The ID baseline variant (order 5) is enabled only when the environment variable testBaseline is set to any value; it swaps InconsistencyChecker for InconsistencyBaseline, whose informant reports a TEAM inconsistency with empty name and fixed confidence 0.69 for every sentence that has no trace link, and it logs the weighted-average metrics without asserting them.

The MEAT evaluation (order 10) reuses the base run's ArdocoResult cached in a static EnumMap by the TEAM run (recomputed if missing) and compares the UIDs of all reported ModelInconsistency instances against the ids listed in the project's *_UME.csv gold standard, logging explicit TP/FP/FN counts without minimum assertions.

InconsistencyDetectionEvaluationIT's javadoc documents the EnumSource names trick for running a single benchmark project — temporarily changing @EnumSource(InconsistencyDetectionTask.class) to include names = { "BIGBLUEBUTTON" } — and warns to revert it before committing.

Evaluation artifacts land under target/testout: ardoco_eval_id/inconsistencies_<PROJECT>.txt and detailed_inconsistencies_<PROJECT>.txt (per hold-back run with removed instance, metrics, and TP/FP/FN lists), ardoco_eval_id/inconsistentModelElements_<PROJECT>.txt for MEAT, plus traceLinks_<PROJECT>.txt and inconsistencyDetection_<PROJECT>.txt for the base run; TLR ITs write runner outputs to target/<project>-output and SwattrAiIT to target/testout-tlr-it-llm.

tlr/update_integration_tests.sh refreshes the tests-tlr tree from the separate ardoco/IntegrationTests repository by adding the integrationTests remote, fetching main, and running git subtree pull --prefix tests/integration-tests integrationTests main --squash.

The documentation-to-code TLR evaluations share AbstractDocumentationToCodeTlrEvaluation, whose confusion-matrix denominator is the number of input text lines × the code-model endpoints; this differs from ArcotlEvaluation's SAM-Code denominator (code-model endpoints × architecture-model endpoints), and the LLM variants built on this base (ExArchEvaluation, ArtemisInTransarcEvaluation, ArtemisInExArchEvaluation) log their results without asserting metrics.

The pipeline modules carry Surefire runner smoke tests built on RunnerBaseTest, which pipeline-core ships in a test-jar (maven-jar-plugin test-jar goal, installed with classifier tests via maven-install-plugin): the base class copies the TeaStore fixtures (text, PCM repository, UML model, additionalConfig.txt) into a fresh temp directory per test class, cleans target/testout-<TestClass> in @AfterEach, and exposes testRunnerAssertions; pipeline-tlr consumes the test-jar test-scoped and pipeline-id obtains it through its default test-dependencies profile.

CodeRunnerBaseTest extends RunnerBaseTest with a TeaStore codeModel.acm CodeConfiguration and, when the environment variable testCodeFull is set, switches to a full shallow clone of the TeaStore repository at a pinned commit (failing the test if the clone fails) — the second consumer of the testCodeFull gate; the concrete smoke tests are SwattrTest, ArcotlTest, ArdocodeTest, and TransarcTest in pipeline-tlr (SwattrTest and all UML variants @Disabled) and InconsistencyDetectionTest — declared in the file ArDoCoForInconsistencyDetectionTest.java — in pipeline-id, which checks the InconsistencyDetection runner with PCM and UML architecture models.

The inconsistency-detection tree carries the same update_integration_tests.sh as the tlr tree: it adds the integrationTests remote, fetches main, and runs git subtree pull --prefix tests/integration-tests integrationTests main --squash to refresh its test tree from ardoco/IntegrationTests.

CI runs mvn verify through the shared ardoco/actions Maven workflow (the root verify.yml declares deploy: false and empty publish secrets and, unlike the module-tree workflow copies, does not set with-submodules), so the effective CI coverage is the unconditional benchmark ITs — SwattrIT, SwattrAiIT, and the ID TEAM/MEAT evaluations — while every @Disabled or env-gated variant stays out: the ArTEMiS/ExArch/LLM ID ITs are @Disabled with OPENAI_API_KEY/OLLAMA_HOST assumptions, the full-clone variants need testCodeFull, the ID baseline needs testBaseline, and the multi-run ArTEMiS variants need mutipleRuns.

The per-approach task enums resolve the gold standards and model inputs: DocumentationToArchitectureModelTlrTask (SAD→SAM CSV, sentence number ↔ model element id) feeds SwattrEvaluationProject and ArtemisEvaluationProject; ModelToCodeTlrTask (three-column SAM→Code CSV, architecture element id ↔ code path where a trailing '/' marks a package) feeds ArcotlEvaluationProject; DocumentationToCodeTlrTask and DocumentationToModelToCodeTlrTask (sentence number ↔ code path; the latter also exposes the architecture model for TransArC) feed ArdocodeEvaluationProject, TransarcEvaluationProject, and the ExArch/ArTEMiS variant project enums; every parser strips the header line and blank lines.

The manual-only InconsistencyDetectionEvaluationArtemisIT (LLM hard-coded to GPT_5_5) evaluates ArTEMiS-based MEAT and TEAM inconsistency detection over three task enums — ComponentArtemisInconsistencyTask (five classic PCM projects with project-specific ExpectedResults), ClassArtemisInconsistencyTask (TEAMMATES, SCONS, BEETS, ZENGARDEN), and DatafileArtemisInconsistencyTask (CORONAWARNAPP, BIGBLUEBUTTON, ROD, TEAMMATES; the latter two with uniform 0.420 minimums) — in six ordered tests. An ArtemisInconsistencyEvaluationConfiguration pins the entity type's ArtemisNerStrategy; run producers all execute via ArtemisInconsistencyRunSupport, which sets up an ArtemisInconsistencyDetection runner (ArtemisPreprocessing, ArtemisNer, connection generation, ArtemisInconsistencyChecker) with outputs under target/testout/artemis-id-runs.

The ArTEMiS ID run producers implement ArtemisInconsistencyRunProducer and differ in hold-back strategy: SingleArtemisInconsistencyRunProducer produces only the base run; ComponentHoldBackArtemisInconsistencyRunProducer iterates the PCM components with HoldBackArCoTLModelProvider and excludes the held-back component from the NER candidate list via HoldBackComponentArtemisNerStrategy; ClassHoldBackArtemisInconsistencyRunProducer runs seeded runs (IT: 3 runs withholding 2 classes each, seed 42) selecting classes from the TLR gold standard with a rarity-weighted random draw (weight = 1/occurrences^0.5) and filters the held-back classes in the connection stage via HoldbackClassArtemisConnectionInformant; DatafileExtendedArtemisInconsistencyRunProducer runs the five SAD extension texts. Run keys are ArtemisEvaluationRun records (BaseEvaluationRun, HeldBackArchitectureItemRun, HeldBackClassesRun, ExtendedSadRun) exposing id, displayName, and isBaseRun.

The ArTEMiS ID evaluators implement ArtemisInconsistencyEvaluator: ComponentArtemisInconsistencyEvaluator compares MEAT (ModelEntityAbsentFromTextInconsistency UIDs vs the *_UME.csv list) and TEAM (trace-link sentences pointing at the held-back component plus sentences of unlinked named entities vs the gold sentences for that component) with the preprocessed text-line count as denominator; ClassArtemisInconsistencyEvaluator compares detected class TEAM sentences (package prefixes stripped) against the class TEAM gold standard, extended by the held-back classes' gold links in the hold-back variant; DatafileArtemisInconsistencyEvaluator compares detected datafile TEAM sentences against the datafile gold standard, extended by goldstandard-extension-N.csv links in the extended variant. ArtemisInconsistencyEvaluationWriter persists results under target/testout/artemis_eval_id as TEAM_<CONFIG>_<PROJECT>.txt / MEAT_<CONFIG>_<PROJECT>.txt with TP/FP/FN sets and weighted averages; nothing asserts minimums.

The @Disabled LLM-validated ID evaluation ITs ArchitecturalStylePatternInconsistencyDetectionEvaluationIT and ProgrammingLanguageInconsistencyDetectionEvaluationIT fix LLM = GPT_5_5 for NER and VALIDATION_AGENT_LLM = GPT_5_4_MINI for the validation agent, parameterize over their task enums × CodeConfigurationType (DIRECTORY from getCodeDirectory or ACM_FILE from bundled resources), and run three variants each: inconsistency detection (validation-agent invalid statements vs the gold standard's valid=false entries), the extended variant (five runs over text-extension resources, weighted-average aggregated, disabled when mutipleRuns is set), and NER (all recognized occurrences vs all gold entries). They compute metrics with a null confusion-matrix sum (the number of distinct styles/languages is not fixed), only log against the loose 0.420 ExpectedResults, and the style/pattern evaluation normalizes LLM names to canonical forms before comparing.

The text-extension resource sets drive the extended LLM-based evaluations: datafile-artemis-text-extensions (bigbluebutton, coronawarnapp, rod, teammates) is shared between tests-inconsistency and tests-tlr and pairs extension-0.txt..extension-4.txt with goldstandard-extension-0.csv..goldstandard-extension-4.csv whose links are appended to the regular gold standard; architectural-style-pattern-text-extensions (beets, coronawarnapp, rod, teammates) and programming-language-text-extensions (rod, scons, teammates, zengarden) follow the same naming with valid/invalid gold entries. The READMEs document LLM generation (gpt-5.6-terra) with the prompts, the datafile README the 5×10 plausible-filename selection, and the programming-language README the six template sentence types with a fixed seed.

The per-entity ArTEMiS TLR evaluations share AbstractArtemisEvaluation (extending AbstractEvaluation): subclasses provide an ArtemisNerStrategy, an Artemis runner, the trace-link string conversion, and the confusion-matrix denominator; the base class runs the runner, reads the ArtemisConnectionState for the strategy's target, enrolls the code gold standard, computes metrics, logs against the project's ExpectedResults, and asserts them via compareResults. ComponentArtemisEvaluation uses the five PCM projects, ClassArtemisEvaluation and DatafileArtemisEvaluation use the cached ACM fixture (sentences × classes and sentences × code files), and DatafileExtensionArtemisEvaluation overrides the documentation file with the datafile text extensions and adds their gold links before scoring.

The LLM-dependent manual-execution evaluations rely on the shared LLM machinery: LargeLanguageModel.create() wraps the provider in CachedChatLanguageModel, which persists prompt-response pairs per model variant to a JSON file under LLM_CACHE_DIR (default .cache-llm/), so repeated manual runs replay cached responses; the ArtemisIT multi-run tests warn that repeated-run averaging is not meaningful if the LLM is cached.
